description: Kansas Legal Services screens requests for civil legal help by telephone and an online intake process. State any court deadline when applying.
introduction: Kansas Legal Services screens requests for civil legal help by telephone and an online intake process. State any court deadline when applying.

sections.who: The organization helps qualifying low- and moderate-income Kansans. Screening considers household finances, the legal problem and available services; the intake team decides what help can be offered.
sections.get: Services include civil issues such as housing, benefits, employment and family matters. Self-help forms and referrals are also available.
sections.docs: Prepare notices, court dates, the opposing party’s name, household income and relevant expenses. Keep copies of everything already filed.
sections.apply:
1. Call 316-267-3975, Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m. The main Get Help page lists online intake from Monday 8 a.m. through Thursday 4:30 p.m.; check the online application’s current status.

  2. Complete follow-up screening. Watch for a call or email from intake and explain urgent deadlines promptly.
sections.after: Confirm whether advice, representation or a referral is offered. Contacting intake does not change a court deadline. Ask who will file any required response.
sections.sources:

faqs: Is there a separate intake number for older adults?
The Elder Law Hotline uses the same main number: 316-267-3975.
Does online intake stay open over the weekend?
No. The Get Help page lists Thursday 4:30 p.m. to Monday 8 a.m. as closed.
Do I need the opposing party’s name?
Yes. Intake asks about the other side of the legal problem.
Will every applicant receive a lawyer?
No. The office screens eligibility and service availability.
